messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: P1 - prod-us-west - high p99 latency > 1200ms across /v1/generate routes. Pager: @jamal-oncall. Alert groups: latency, downstream timeouts.
jamal-oncall: On it. Starting live mitigation: divert 20% traffic to dedicated pool, scale replica count +2, purging KV cache on warm nodes. Will watch 1m.
ben-sre: Acknowledged. Any 5xx/customer-facing errors seen yet?
jamal-oncall: Seeing a small spike in 502s for requests > 8k tokens. Most customers slowed; two customers opened support tickets (acme-corp, globex). No full region outage.
lucy-monitoring: Pasted quick query for what I'm watching: 
```
sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{env="prod",route=~"/v1/generate.*"}[1m])) by (route)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env="prod"}[5m])) by (le, route))
sum(gpu_utilization_percent{region="us-west"}) by (instance)
kv_cache_hitratio{env="prod"}
```
lucy-monitoring: If KV hitrate drops that explains token regen overhead. Also seeing queue length grow on frontend LB.
alice-oconnor: For the post-incident retro/dashboard we should include: 99/95/50 latency, request rate, queued requests, GPU util, KV hitrate, per-customer 5xx, and top slow routes. Drilldown panels to go from route -> customer -> sample requests.
ben-sre: Agree. Golden signals: latency(p50/p95/p99), errors (5xx rate and percentage), saturation (GPU util, queue depth). Add a panel for model fallback events and routing fallbacks.
jamal-oncall: Live note: scaled and diverted reduced p99 by ~200ms. 502s still trickling. I'll keep mitigation for 10m then start handoff.
sre-rotation-bot: Handoff scheduled: @alex-next will take on-call at 3350011400 UTC.
jamal-oncall: Handoff to @alex-next at 3350011400 — leaving runbook notes: 1) check p99 on /v1/generate 2) confirm no backlog > 2k reqs 3) ensure dedicated pool autoscaler healthy.
sam-product: Do we need customer comms? I can draft a short status page update and proactive emails for the two impacted customers.
jamal-oncall: Yes please. Short note + ETA for followup. I'll annotate impact and timeline in the incident doc.
lucy-monitoring: Alert tuning proposals (temp): 
- Increase prod-us-west p99 latency alert threshold from 1200ms -> 1500ms for 5m window to reduce noisy pages while we investigate.
- Add a new alert: per-customer 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained 5m for major customers.
- Create anomaly rule for queue growth > 30% over 3m.
Reasoning: Most noise was in short-lived bursts tied to cache misses and routing thrash. We'll revert thresholds after dashboard and followup.

alice-oconnor: Dashboard owner/PR plan: @jamal-oncall will open a grafana dashboard PR with panels + drilldown links. @alice-oconnor will review layout, @lucy-monitoring will validate queries. Timeline: PR by EOD, review tomorrow.
jamal-oncall: I'll open the PR after handoff. Draft name: "incident-retro-p99-latency-us-west". Will include sample queries, panel descriptions, and runbook links.
ben-sre: For drilldowns, add a table panel with top 20 slow traces and a link to the request inspector. Add templating for customer ID to filter quickly.
lucy-monitoring: Also add a small panel for backend queue distribution and a heatmap of token counts vs latency — helps spot long-token regressions.
jamal-oncall: Action items: 
- Jamal: open grafana PR + mitigation notes (in progress)
- Alice: review dashboard UX
- Lucy: add queries and alert rule diffs
- Sam: draft customer comms
- Alex: follow up on autoscaler logs after handoff

jamal-oncall: FYI opening placeholder PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/grafana-dashboards/pull/387 (will update with panels) :memo:
alex-next: Taking over on-call. Thanks @jamal-oncall — I'll validate the autoscaler, check for residual queueing, and monitor customer tickets.
ben-sre: Post-incident: let's do 1) dashboard PR, 2) alert tuning PR, 3) runbook tweak for KV-cache cold start. Recommend a small postmortem meeting tomorrow.
jamal-oncall: Agreed. I'll link the incident doc and calendar invite. Ending live thread — will post final retro notes and assign followups. :white_check_mark:
